A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same wrong-event-based label-noise learning framework. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices are readable and support comparison, including matching v1 Appendices A–C to reorganized material in v3.

before.justification: v1 reports original classification experiments, runtime comparisons, metric and loss ablations, and appendix hyperparameter-sensitivity experiments.

after.justification: v3 retains original classification experiments and adds clean-sample selection measurements, runtime breakdowns, and initialization and accumulated-loss comparisons.

M1.justification: v3 adds a confidence coefficient c = max(f(x_i)) to the noisy-sample loss in Equation 11; v1 Equation 12 lacks this factor. The two-stage procedure, classwise beta-mixture modeling, and other loss components remain substantially unchanged. Renaming DODO to IDO is separate from this actual loss modification.

E1.justification: v3 extends CIFAR-10 evaluation to additional noise conditions, including 20% and 60% symmetric noise in Table 16. CIFAR-10 itself already appears in v1's diagnostic experiments, so it is not an entirely new dataset. The remaining datasets and image-classification domain are retained; Clothing1M-F/R distinguish sampling protocols.

E2.justification: Most comparison methods remain. v3 adds DMix and UNICON results to the existing Tiny-ImageNet comparison, adds UNICON to the scalability comparison, and evaluates M-Correction in Table 13. It removes the separate ELR* CLIP-ViT-B/16 row from Table 2.

E3.justification: v3 introduces fixed-subset and per-epoch-resampled Clothing1M evaluations, plus threshold-based precision/recall/F-score and AUC protocols. Table 4 removes the 16-epoch condition, while Table 3 removes symmetric-noise evaluations and adds peak GPU memory measurements. Runtime hardware changes from a stated A100 40GB to 80GB. Figures 2 and 6 also revise their stated noise rates; these documentation changes do not establish reruns.

E4.justification: New analyses examine inter-epoch metric changes, clean-sample selection, fitting-time overhead, continuing from the base model versus restarting, and accumulated loss with BMM/GMM versus wrong event (Figure 7 and Tables 9–15). These substantially expand investigation of the method's mechanisms. The ELR/DivideMix sensitivity studies already existed in v1 Appendix C and are moved to v3 Appendix A.

E5.justification: v1 Table 1 reports averages over three random trials; v3 Section 5.1 reports five-run averages across experiments. This changes the stated repetition count and reporting scope. Neither version reports corresponding run-to-run confidence intervals or significance tests; the existing distribution plots already show medians and interquartile ranges.

E6.justification: Numerous reported values change: Table 1's proposed-method ResNet-50 accuracy on CIFAR-100 Sym. 60% changes from 81.0% to 81.4%, while TURN on Tiny-ImageNet Sym. 20% changes from 75.2% to 70.2%. v3 adds classification, selection, memory, timing, and ablation results and removes some evaluation entries. Clothing1M scores are reorganized into protocol-specific results and should not be interpreted as simple same-setting gains.

T1.justification: Beyond v1's mainly intuitive robustness discussion, v3 adds explicit difficulty bounds and a purported proof of decreasing wrong-event variation in Appendix C.2. The new relative-change bound of 1/T is invalid under Equation 1: when w_T = 1 and w_(T+1) = 2, the relative change is 1 even for T > 1. This is a substantive mathematical addition, with a correctness problem.

C1.justification: The central two-stage, instance-level denoising contribution remains. v3 adds an explicit first-use claim for probabilistic difficulty modeling, emphasizes operation with or without pretraining, and extends the abstract's nearly 75% reduction claim from computation time to storage as well. The introduction's claimed synthetic/real-world accuracy margins change from 1.1%/0.8% to 1.6%/0.7%.

C2.justification: Appendices D–E add explanations for fitting efficiency, initialization effects, accumulated-loss behavior, and smaller improvements on real-world noise. Appendix F newly identifies noise rates above 90% as a failure condition and discusses application and annotation-workforce implications. These substantially expand the interpretation and applicability qualifications beyond v1.

D1.justification: v3 supplies a code-access URL and newly documents BMM initialization, fitting iterations and reuse without reinitialization, scalability batch size, and Clothing1M sampling and wrong-event updates every 100 iterations. These fill important implementation gaps without establishing that previously unspecified procedures changed. Most optimizer and baseline hyperparameters remain, although v1's explicit max-normalization description for wrong event is omitted.

R1.justification: v3 adds references including Self-filtering, Beyond Synthetic Noise, and a noisy-label learning survey, plus additional introduction citations; CurriculumNet is removed. The existing research positioning largely remains, with added discussion of fluctuation events and a stronger first-use claim for probabilistic difficulty modeling.

P1.justification: The introduction is extensively rewritten around distinguishing noisy and difficult examples, and Section 3 is retitled and reorganized. DODO becomes IDO, related-work explanations are revised, and references move before a reorganized supplementary section with a roadmap and Appendices A–F. These are substantial narrative and structural changes beyond the added experiments.

P2.justification: v3 substantially reorganizes displays: Figures 1 and 4 become smaller wrapped figures, Tables 3 and 4 appear side by side, and Tables 2–3 gain revised column structures. Figure 7 and Tables 9–16 add new displays. Distribution-axis labels are revised, but Figure 4 incorrectly changes its accuracy-axis label to 'Number of Examples'.

improvement.justification: v3 strengthens empirical support through selection diagnostics, targeted ablations, and runtime decomposition, while adding useful implementation details and an explicit limitation. However, its new Appendix C.2 introduces an invalid relative-change bound and presents inter-epoch changes as a variance proof, weakening the reliability of its strengthened theoretical claims. These substantive benefits and new correctness problems leave the overall quality direction uncertain.
